sources.title: LLC ownership structure: Members, profits, and control explained - Stripe
sources.snippet:
## Who owns an LLC?
Owners are called members and each member owns a stake in the LLC itself, not the company’s individual [assets](https://stripe.com/resources/more/asset-verification-101-what-it-is-how-it-works-and-what-it-is-used-for).

Ownership doesn’t require day-to-day participation. Adding a new member often requires approval from existing members. This preserves control over who becomes an owner and prevents unwanted ownership transfers.

The combination of two agreements decides the exact structure.

sources.snippet:
# What does LLC mean, and is it right for your business?
![/](https://www.citizensbank.com/dam/f6583c97-facd-4d3c-b3a3-aec2005b2c3d/GettyImages-496033159_H1Hero.jpg)

## Key takeaways
- LLC stands for limited liability company, which means its members are not personally liable for the company’s debts.
- LLCs are taxed on a “pass-through” basis — all profits and losses are filed through the member’s personal tax return.
- Generally, LLCs are required to pay a one-time filing fee as well as an annual fee. However, some states do not require an annual fee.
